title: Grow a Landscaping Business: From Gardener to Builder
meta_description: How to grow a landscaping business past £500k: sell design and build projects rather than day labour, kill the winter dip, and upsell maintenance on every job.
h1: Grow a Landscaping Business: From Gardener to Builder
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to moving from patios and maintenance to full garden builds.

intro.answer: You can mow lawns all year and still be skint. The businesses that break past £500k stop thinking like a gardener and start operating like a construction business.

image.alt: A completed landscaping project built as a full outdoor construction job

intro.roadmap: This guide covers the shift from jobs to projects: selling design and build rather than labour, building revenue that survives January, using visual marketing properly, upselling maintenance on every project, and systemising the whole thing like a contractor would.

briefing.title: The Problem Is Positioning, Not Pricing
briefing.intro: A landscaper turning over just under £500k, great reputation, brilliant workmanship, pricing £8k to £15k patios all day and competing on price. Diary full, bank account not. Nothing about the work needed fixing. What needed fixing was what clients thought he was.

panels.heading: Why does a busy landscaping business stay skint?
paragraphs: Because it is selling jobs rather than projects. A patio is a job: priced against the bloke down the road, won on price, finished in a fortnight. A garden transformation is a project, priced on the outcome and judged on the design.

He saw himself as a landscaper. His clients saw him as a bloke who does patios. Once he was reframed as an outdoor construction specialist offering full garden transformations, the conversation changed and so did the numbers.

panels.heading: The five moves that make the shift
paragraphs: Each one lifts the average project value or takes the seasonality out of the year.
steps: Sell design and build packages, not just labour.
Build year round revenue so January is not a panic.
Use visual marketing properly, because this trade sells on the photograph.
Upsell a maintenance contract on every project you finish.
Systemise it like a construction company rather than a gardening round.

review.label: The real upgrade
review.text: None of this is about working harder or charging more for the same thing. It is about being bought as a different kind of business, which changes who calls you and what they expect to pay.
